items.title: [Perf] deepseek-v4: DSpark draft stages take the TF32 mHC statistics path from 32 rows on SM100
items.body:
## Motivation

Under DSpark decode, the three draft stages compute the mixing statistics of their six mHC boundaries with the Triton split-K kernel (`hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn`) at every batch, while the target layers run DeepGEMM's `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` from 128 rows. Two reasons: the DSpark model never calls `refresh_mhc_norm_weight_cache`, so its stages have no TF32 weight parts, and `_mix_stats_impl` keeps the DeepGEMM path off under 128 rows on SM100 (SM90 uses it from 32).

Measured on GB300 (DEP16 decode, DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash, 128K contexts, torch profiler, kernel durations):

| Draft rows (= requests per rank) | `_hc_mix_stats_partial_kernel`, 6 launches | `_hc_mix_reduce_sinkhorn_kernel`, 6 launches | Per cycle |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 | 6 x 23.8 us | 6 x 9.0 us | 0.197 ms |
| 64 | 6 x 42.2 us | 6 x 9.1 us | 0.307 ms |
| 256 | 6 x 150 us | 6 x 10.5 us | 0.963 ms |

In the same traces the target's unfused boundaries run `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_impl` at 7.4-7.9 us per launch (160 and 320 rows) plus a 16-slice reduce of 7.8 us: about 23 us per boundary against 52 us on the Triton path at 64 rows. The 128-row floor is not a kernel requirement: DeepGEMM's SM100 kernel uses `block_m = 64` with a grid of `num_splits x ceil_div(m, 64)` and no assertion on M.

## Modifications

- `DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark.post_load_weights` calls `refresh_mhc_norm_weight_cache` on each stage, which builds the TF32 parts of the 24 x 20,480 mixing weights (24 MB per GPU for three stages).
- `_mix_stats_impl`: the row floor for the TF32 parts becomes 32 on SM100 as on SM90 (`x_flat.shape[0] >= 32` replaces `>= 128 or hopper_medium`, which already meant 32 on SM90). Batch-invariant mode and rows under 32 are unchanged.

Expected: about 0.17 ms less per decode cycle at 64 requests per rank (22.6 ms cycle), 0.06 ms at 32.

## Accuracy Tests

The draft's statistics move from the Triton tf32x3 kernel to the two-part TF32 split the target already runs at 128 rows and above. Accept length from the A/B decode logs will be posted here; GSM8K at native acceptance on request.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The A/B at 64 requests per rank (same recipe, base main 49766a74f9 against this branch) is running; the six draft launches and the log cycle will be posted here.

items.title: [CI] base-b: Move kernel and unit tests that pass on the 5090 to 1-gpu-small
items.body:
## Summary

Second of the series that splits #41231 into reviewable PRs, one CI lane each (first: #44876). This one moves 27 light base-b test files (kernels/ops, moe, unit, layers, mem_cache, model_loading, prefill_only) from 1-gpu-large (H100) to 1-gpu-small (RTX 5090). Every change is the `runner_config` of one `register_cuda_ci` line, with `est_time` set to the measured 5090 duration where the estimate was more than 1.5x low. `test_nvfp4_marlin` was already registered on 1-gpu-small (est_time 12, 11s measured); its 1-gpu-large duplicate is dropped.

Rule for a file to move: it passes on the 5090 (SM120, 32 GB) with the CI install and env, every test it skips on the 5090 also skips on H100, and where it launches a server, any architecture-dependent default it picks up (e.g. FA3 on H100 vs FlashInfer on SM120) is not what the test is about. No coverage is lost.

| base-b per-commit est_time | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1-gpu-large | 129 files / 175.4 min | 101 / 168.1 min |
| 1-gpu-small | 150 files / 191.9 min | 177 / 205.8 min |

Partitions are sized from est_time by `compute_partitions.py`, so no workflow change is needed. Independent of #44876 (no shared files).

## Validation

All 30 candidate files passed on the 1-gpu-5090 runners at `8d58a33e16` with `/rerun-test -c` ([run 39021620314](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39021620314)), then compared with the same files on H100 in main's scheduled run:

- `test_mhc_kernels` stays on 1-gpu-large: 33 passed, 16 skipped on the 5090 vs 49 passed on H100. The skipped cases are its `test_hopper_*` functions, which exercise the SM90-only mHC dispatch.
- Same skips on both: `test_topk_padded_region` (3), `test_fp8_utils` (1). `test_flash_mla_backends` skips all 15 cases on H100 and runs 14 on the 5090.
- `test_post_capture_kv_sizing` is the only file that starts a server; it gets FlashInfer on the 5090 instead of FA3. Post-capture KV sizing has no attention-backend-specific path, and the run confirms the sizing path ran.

Merged main `5e630fa571` into the branch: main deleted `kernels/ops/gemm/test_fp8_kernel.py` (#44690), so it is no longer part of this PR. Main changed 9 of the other files since the run above, so all 28 are being rerun on the 5090 with `/rerun-test -c`.

## Follow-ups

extra-a, the round-4 class splits, the jit-kernel unit / benchmark lanes and diffusion follow as separate PRs; #41231 tracks them.

items.title: [Perf] dsv41: Speed up decode-size mHC mixing with a vectorized split-K reduce and 160 K slices on SM120
items.body:
## Motivation

`hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn` is the CUDA Triton path for DeepSeek-V4.x mHC mixing statistics and Sinkhorn, run twice per layer. It is used at every row count on SM120, on SM100 when the DeepGEMM prenorm GEMM is not used (including below 128 rows), and on SM90 at one row. It has two launches:

1. `_hc_mix_stats_partial_kernel`: one CTA per (row tile, K slice). K=20480 is split into 80 slices.
2. `_hc_mix_reduce_sinkhorn_kernel`: one single-warp CTA per row, which adds the 80 slice partials in a serial `static_range` loop before the Sinkhorn.

At decode sizes the serial loop takes about as long as the partial kernel. With one row tile, 80 CTAs also occupy fewer than half of the 188 SMs on an RTX PRO 6000.

## Modifications

- `_hc_mix_reduce_sinkhorn_vec_kernel`: loads the partials as one `[slices, cols]` tile and reduces them with `tl.sum`, then runs the unchanged Sinkhorn. There is still one CTA per row, and the reduction tree depends only on the slice count, so results are deterministic and batch-invariant. The summation order differs from the serial loop. `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn` uses it on SM120 (compute capability 12.0), where it was measured; other GPUs keep the serial reducer, so their results are unchanged. The bf16x3 and DeepGEMM paths keep the serial reducer with 16 slices; DeepGEMM also keeps its residual input.
- `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn(..., decode=False)`: with `decode=True` on SM120 (compute capability 12.0 only), it splits K into 160 slices when the number of 64-wide K blocks is a multiple of 160. `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.forward_hc_pre_from_prev` sets `decode` for decode/idle and target-verify forward passes and passes it through `mhc.run_attn_post` / `run_moe_post`, `_compute_triplet`, `mix_stats` and `_mix_stats_impl` to `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn`. Each new `decode` parameter defaults to False. Prefill/extend, other callers (including the DSpark draft layer, which calls `mix_stats` directly), other GPUs, and the unfused `hc_mix_stats` keep the existing choice (80 for K=20480). The slice count depends on K, the device, and the forward mode, never on M. A row therefore gets the same bits at any batch size within decode/verify on this backend, and likewise within prefill. A decode row can also run beside prefill rows in a MIXED batch, which takes the prefill split, so with batch-invariant mode enabled (`--enable-deterministic-inference`) `_mix_stats_impl` passes `decode=False` in every mode, as it already disables the compensated projections in that mode.

## Accuracy Tests

New `test_hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn.py` (GPU) and `test_deepseek_v4_mhc_decode_split.py` (CPU). With this branch head's `mhc.py` and tests, all 23 tests in `test_hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn.py` passed on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), and the 4 tests in `test_deepseek_v4_mhc_decode_split.py` passed on CPU. I have not run the ported model code end to end on a GPU (`deepseek_v4.py`, `deepseek_v4_mhc.py` on current main). The tests cover:
- Slice selection: 160 for decode and 80 for prefill on SM120; 80 for both on SM100 and SM121; 80 for a K whose 64-wide block count is not a multiple of 160.
- Accuracy: K=20480 in decode mode at M = 1, 6, 48 and 300 (160 slices) and in prefill mode at M = 6 and 300 (80 slices), plus K = 5120, 4096 and 192 (80, 64 and 1 slices). The fused op matches the unfused `hc_mix_stats` (serial sum, 80 slices at K=20480) followed by the Sinkhorn within rtol 1e-5 / atol 1e-6. It also matches FP64 mixing statistics followed by the FP32 Sinkhorn within rtol 1e-4 / atol 1e-5.
- Determinism and batch invariance in each mode, with the device forced to SM120 (vectorized reduce) and to SM100 (serial reduce) on any host GPU, as in the accuracy cases. The test checks the selected reducer and slice count, that repeated calls are bitwise equal, and that rows computed alone, as the first 8, 9, 2048 and 2049, and as every 7th of a 2056-row batch are bitwise equal to the same rows in that batch. These subsets use all three row tiles (8, 16 and 32 rows; 32 starts at 2049 rows).
- Model wiring, on CPU with a mocked layer and no weights: the real `forward_hc_pre_from_prev`, posts and `mix_stats` pass `decode=True` to `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn` for both hyper-connections in decode, idle and target-verify forward passes, and `decode=False` in extend, mixed, draft-extend and split-prefill passes. With batch-invariant mode enabled, every forward mode passes `decode=False`, so decode and MIXED batches select the same slice count (80 on SM120). A direct `mix_stats` call defaults to `decode=False`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Per call (partial + reduce/Sinkhorn, `us`) on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (SM120, 188 SMs, 250 W power limit, used only by the benchmark), torch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. Inputs are BF16 `[M, 20480]`. Each CUDA graph covers 24 distinct `[24, 20480]` FP32 weights at M <= 64 and 4 weights above; the time is the best of 20 graph replays divided by the number of calls. Columns:
- main: `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn` from the base commit's `mhc.py` (serial reduce, 80 slices);
- `decode=False`: this PR's `mhc.py` (vectorized reduce, 80 slices);
- `decode=True`: this PR's `mhc.py` (vectorized reduce, 160 slices, the SM120 decode/verify setting);
- max abs diff: the largest absolute difference over the `pre`, `post` and `comb` outputs between `decode=True` and main, for the first weight.

| M | main | `decode=False` | `decode=True` | max abs diff |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8.45 | 7.59 | 6.23 | 2.38e-07 |
| 2 | 9.97 | 7.74 | 6.52 | 2.38e-07 |
| 4 | 10.08 | 7.77 | 6.57 | 3.58e-07 |
| 8 | 10.18 | 7.84 | 6.66 | 2.38e-07 |
| 16 | 11.02 | 8.56 | 7.21 | 2.38e-07 |
| 32 | 11.20 | 8.78 | 8.22 | 3.58e-07 |
| 48 | 12.54 | 10.17 | 10.60 | 3.58e-07 |
| 64 | 12.76 | 10.42 | 10.97 | 3.58e-07 |
| 96 | 15.53 | 13.28 | 13.85 | 3.58e-07 |
| 128 | 19.46 | 17.21 | 16.35 | 3.58e-07 |
| 256 | 27.24 | 25.13 | 26.02 | 5.36e-07 |

With 80 slices, the vectorized reduce lowers latency by 8-23% versus main at every M measured. With 160 slices, latency is a further 15-18% lower up to 16 rows (26-35% lower than main) and 6% lower at 32 rows. At 48-256 rows, 160 slices changes latency by -5% to +5% relative to 80 slices (these sizes occur in large verify batches) and is 4-16% lower than main.

I measured the following with the same kernel change on my branch before the port onto #42245, and have not repeated them on this port.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (PCIe), TP4/EP2, DSpark speculative decoding:
- Vectorized reduce: the reduce took 6.0 -> 3.5 us per call at 6 rows. End-to-end decode throughput (median of 3 runs, temperature 1) on two consecutive builds, the second adding this reduce, changed by -0.5 / -1.6 / +3.5 / +0.1% at 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 concurrent requests.
- 160 slices: in a decode profile, the mix partial kernel took 9.0 -> 6.5 us per call.

160 slices is limited to SM120 decode/verify, the only architecture and mode where I measured it; I have no same-build prefill A/B, so prefill keeps 80 slices.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

items.title: [Feat] volundr: Add Agens Volundr model support
items.body:
## Motivation

Agens Volundr (`Blockway/Agens-Volundr-32B-v1`, `Blockway/Agens-Volundr-32B-v1-INT4` (W4A16)) is a hybrid model that
today only runs from a patched SGLang build (`ghcr.io/blockwayz/agens-sglang:v1-sm89` / `v1-sm90`). This PR adds native support so a stock install serves it.

Architecture, as the runtime sees it:

- **KDA** linear-attention layers (per-channel forget gate), served by the existing `KDAAttnBackend`
  through `RadixLinearAttention`, with grouped value attention (48 value heads over 16 key heads).
- **BCSA** layers: a 4,096-token sliding window plus a 4:1 mean-pooled far field chosen by a learned
  128-wide indexer, merged with the window under one softmax through the window's LSE. The indexer key
  depends on the layer input, so each BCSA layer keeps a per-token side cache indexed by
  `out_cache_loc` like K/V. One `attn` layer is plain dense attention.
- **mHC** (manifold hyper-connections): 4 residual streams with Sinkhorn-normalised mixing around
  every layer.
- **Engram**: hashed n-gram memory on two layers; needs the two previous token ids of every token.
- Optional vision tower: SGLang's qwen3_vl vision model and MRoPE, unchanged.

The layer map comes from `config.mixer_types`; the attention layers do not sit on a fixed interval.

## Modifications

New files

- `srt/models/volundr.py` — `VolundrForCausalLM`, `VolundrForConditionalGeneration`. Weights load
  as shipped (HF names; `gate_up_proj` stacking; blockwise column-parallel loaders for the fused
  `[q|k|v]` projection and conv at tp > 1). Every attention/MLP RMSNorm is the zero-centred
  `GemmaRMSNorm`; mHC and the KDA output norm are plain.
- `srt/configs/volundr.py` — `VolundrTextConfig` (layer map from `mixer_types`, KDA state layout via
  `KimiLinearCacheParams`, BCSA/Engram/mHC fields with defaults), `VolundrConfig` (vision + text);
  registered in `_CONFIG_REGISTRY` and the linear-attention model registry (-> `KDAAttnBackend`).
- `kernels/ops/layernorm/volundr_mhc.py`, `kernels/ops/attention/volundr_bcsa.py` — Triton kernels for
  mHC mix/combine and the BCSA decode block-key write / far branch (~6,000 small launches per decode
  step become a few per layer). Each is bit-exact with the torch reference next to it; the rounding
  rules that make it so (libdevice exp, `div_rn`, fixed reduction order, FMA contraction off) are in
  the module docstrings. Registered for the kernel inventory.
- `srt/function_call/agens_detector.py` — `AgensDetector` (Qwen3-Coder XML body inside
  `<|call|>`/`<|/call|>`).
- `arg_groups/model_overrides/volundr.py` — defaults: `page_size=1` (BCSA pools far-field K/V straight
  from the token-indexed cache), `--attention-backend fa3`.

Edits to shared files (all small)

- `configs/hybrid_arch.py`: an explicit linear-attention registration wins over the `Qwen3Next`
  isinstance chain in `hybrid_gdn_config` (Volundr's config reuses the Qwen3.5 text-config plumbing,
  but its linear layers are KDA, not GDN).
- `configs/model_config.py`: `uses_kda_attention` also recognises registry entries whose backend is
  `KDAAttnBackend` (so the KDA prefill-graph rule applies); multimodal arch lists.
- `layers/attention/linear/kernels/kda_triton.py`: `extend` broadcasts q/k heads when
  `num_v_heads > num_k_heads` (the decode/verify kernels already handle grouped value attention).
- `multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py`: Volundr uses the Qwen3.5 vision/MRoPE path (`vision_config.model_type`).
- Parsers: `AgensDetector` reasoning detector in `parser/reasoning_parser.py` (`<|think|>…<|/think|>`,
  `<|call|>` closes reasoning implicitly), `agens` in both registries and both name lists.
- `sampling/custom_logit_processor.py`: `AgensThinkingBudgetLogitProcessor` (thinking-token ids
  248068/248069, newline 198), used through the existing `custom_params.thinking_budget`.

Behaviour notes

- Token ids listed in the checkpoint's `generation_config.suppress_tokens` (padding rows of the
  embedding/lm_head past the tokenizer) are masked from next-token logits, as transformers'
  `SuppressTokensLogitsProcessor` does. Input logprobs are untouched.
- No environment variables. No `trust_remote_code` needed (the config class is native; a checkpoint
  `auto_map` is ignored by the registry reload).
- In this PR: tp >= 1 bf16, INT4 (compressed-tensors) at tp 1, fa3 backend (sm90). Prefix caching,
  the FlashInfer backend / sm89 and far/near decode graphs, and speculative decoding follow as
  separate PRs.

## Accuracy Tests

Teacher-forced against the checkpoint's own transformers implementation (one HF forward per passage,
dumped once, every engine compared against the same dump). Passages: license texts and Python
sources, 285 / 4,000 / 6,000 / 12,133 tokens. "Disagree" = top-1 differs; the reference's own
top1–top2 logprob margin at those positions is listed. KL20 = KL(ref || engine) over the reference's
top-20 tokens (approximation; engine logprobs outside its own top-20 floored at its 20th).

| bf16, sm90, fa3 | 285 | 4,000 | 6,000 | 12,133 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR, tp1: top-1 | 100.00 % | 99.97 % | 99.93 % | 99.88 % |
| this PR, tp1: mean abs. dlogprob(target) | 0.0016 | 0.0020 | 0.0014 | 0.0021 |
| this PR, tp1: KL20 | 3.3e-4 | 1.5e-4 | 1.1e-4 | 1.7e-4 |
| this PR, tp2: top-1 | 100.00 % | 99.97 % | 99.95 % | 99.90 % |
| previous out-of-tree build, tp1: top-1 | 100.00 % | 99.97 % | 99.93 % | 99.93 % |
| previous out-of-tree build: mean abs. dlogprob | 0.0018 | 0.0023 | 0.0018 | 0.0023 |

All disagreements sit at reference margins of 0.0–0.375 (bf16 ties). The 12,133-token passage has
15 / 12,132 disagreements here vs 9 for the previous build; mean dlogprob and KL20 are lower here.
Decode path vs prefill (greedy-decode 256 tokens on 8 prompts of 300–6,000 tokens, several crossing
the 4,096 window, then teacher-force the same tokens): mean abs. difference 0.0051, 4 / 2,048
top-1 flips (previous build 0.0045, 10 / 2,048). Runs are deterministic (repeat = bit-identical).

Fused kernels: bit-exact against the torch references (`test/registered/kernels/ops/...`).

Serving smoke (bf16 tp1 and INT4 tp1, text and vision checkpoints): `--reasoning-parser agens`
splits reasoning/content (thinking on and off); `--tool-call-parser agens` parses 8/8 sampled
tool calls at T=0.6; `thinking_budget=32` caps reasoning at 32 tokens; an image of three coloured
shapes is described correctly (`--enable-multimodal`).

Long context: one 32,768-token passage, top-1 99.81 % (63 / 32,767 disagreements, all at reference
margins <= 0.375), KL20 2.6e-4; the mean dlogprob grows along the sequence (0.0019 in the first 4K,
0.0055 in the last 4K).

Benchmarks (sm90, bf16 tp1, the v1 model-card protocol):

| | this PR | previous out-of-tree build |
|---|---|---|
| GPQA diamond, 198 items, 6K thinking budget with forced close, T 0.6 / top_p 0.95, 4 runs | 78.3 / 82.3 / 80.8 / 78.8, mean 80.05 | mean 79.3 |
| HumanEval, greedy, 512 tokens | 78.0 | 78.7 |

Tiny-model e2e (`test/registered/e2e/models/test_volundr_tiny.py`, `Blockway/Agens-Volundr-tiny-random`):
teacher-forced top-1 vs HF reference values recorded from the checkpoint's own implementation >= 99 %,
decode-vs-prefill KL ~1e-3.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

sm90 (141 GB), bf16 tp1, fa3, prefix cache off (this PR), idle host:

| | 1K prompt, 1 stream | 8K prompt, 1 stream | 16 x 1K, aggregate incl. prefill | 16 x 1K, steady decode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | 48.7 tok/s | 44.3 | 572.5 | 668.6 |
| previous out-of-tree build | 47.8 | 44.2 | 570 | — |

`sglang.benchmark.one_batch` (model only, CUDA graphs, 1K input): 20.6 ms per decode step at bs 1,
23.9 ms at bs 16 (670 tok/s). INT4 tp1: 67.9 / 67.2 tok/s single stream.

## Checklist

- [x] pre-commit
- [x] Unit tests: `unit/function_call/test_agens_detector.py`, `unit/parser/test_agens_reasoning_parser.py`,
      `unit/configs/test_volundr_config.py`, `kernels/ops/layernorm/test_volundr_mhc.py`,
      `kernels/ops/attention/test_volundr_bcsa.py`; existing parser-name and registry tests pass
- [x] e2e: `test/registered/e2e/models/test_volundr_tiny.py` on `Blockway/Agens-Volundr-tiny-random`
      (2 KDA + 1 BCSA + 1 dense, Engram, mHC, BCSA window 64 so the far field is exercised; 81 MB),
      `register_cuda_ci(stage="extra-a", runner_config="1-gpu-large")`; reference values in
      `volundr_tiny_reference.json` (recorded from the checkpoint's transformers implementation, since
      that implementation needs transformers 5.8 and is not run in CI)
- [ ] Docs: `docs/docs/supported-models/` entry and a cookbook recipe

items.body:
## Motivation

Six months of fast kernel and diffusion work left a lot behind in `python/sglang/kernels`, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen` and the kernel/diffusion test trees: kernels nothing calls, registry metadata nothing reads, per-model copies of the same fused-op glue, env knobs that do nothing, and tests that pass without testing anything. This PR removes that, and fixes the real bugs the audit turned up along the way (several were silently shipping).

**408 files, +3,629 / -26,346.** About 1.3K of the additions are test oracles and helpers moved out of production modules into `python/sglang/test/kernels/`.

## Bugs fixed (please review these first)

| Area | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| SANA (diffusion) | Since #37816 the VAE loader calls `vae.state_dict()` before `load_state_dict`; `AutoencoderDC` builds its inner diffusers model lazily, so that call built it with random init and the later load returned early. **All 375 VAE tensors were random; every SANA T2I image on main is noise.** | `load_state_dict` loads into an already-built inner model. Regression test in `test_vae_loader.py` (fails on main). |
| GLM-Image (diffusion) | #33555 added an unconditional `query[:, t:] = q_img` write-back after an in-place RoPE; torch 2.14 rejects the self-copy, so **every GLM-Image request fails** in the first DiT block. | Copy back only when the rotation returned new memory. Regression test `test_glm_image_attention.py`; `test_ar_models` re-enabled (fails on main, passes here in 175 s on 2xH200). |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE | The default-on `h3_vae_qk_rmsnorm_rope` path ran in `quality=exact` but was not bit-exact (~25% of rotated channels differ). A second, faster, quality-gated fused path for the same op already existed. | Removed the non-bit-exact path. **Behavior change:** the exact tier now runs the native chain (bit-identical to native); lossless is unchanged. |
| Diffusion CI | `STANDALONE_FILES` moved to `server/gpu_cases.py` in #24630 but the CUDA partition planner kept reading the runner, so **no CUDA standalone file has run since June** (12 2-GPU files + the 1-GPU ones). | Planner reads the case config. All 15 newly scheduled files were run on H200 through the CI code path; one rotted test fixed. |
| Env vars | Code read the legacy `SGL_*` names while docs/`environ.py` define `SGLANG_*`, and the rewrite is one-directional, so the documented names did nothing: `SGLANG_USE_DEEPGEMM_BMM` (5 models), `SGLANG_DG_USE_NVRTC`, `SGLANG_CPU_QUANTIZATION`, `SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_ROW_SPLIT`. | Read via `envs`; legacy names still work. |
| `BaseFusedOp` | `KernelBackend.FLYDSL` mapped to a missing `forward_flydsl`, so `SGLANG_FORCE_FUSED_OP_BACKEND=flydsl` raised `AttributeError`. | Stub added + test. |
| Tests that never ran | `test_fp8_kernel` returned early on every CUDA GPU with sm>=90; `test_swapab_attention` was registered on H100 but gated to sm_10x (production SM100 kernel had no CUDA coverage); sm_100 / sm_120 / 2-GPU / 4-GPU diffusion unit tests sat on a 1-GPU H100 lane; `test_qwen_image21` cache tests exercised a test-local re-implementation of the fix. | Each now runs on hardware that satisfies its gate (or was deleted with its dead kernel); the qwen_image21 tests drive the real block and fail when the fix is reverted. |
| SenseNova-U1 | `FlowMatchingHead` called `SimpleMLPAdaLN` with a signature the class doesn't have (crash for `fm_head_layers > 2`). | Restored the timestep-conditioned head; test fails on main. |

## Modifications

### Kernels (`python/sglang/kernels`, -13.8K)
- **Dead / test-only kernels removed** (each re-verified with whole-repo grep incl. string lookups): seg_la kernel, dsv4 `fused_ape_pool_norm_rope`, tilelang `fp8_index`, KDA prefill timing scaffolding, nvlink push/pull all-reduce wrappers, inkling two-shot all-reduce, `cutedsl_gdn_mtp_ring` T=1 entry, non-`f_b` FlyDSL KDA decode, dsa `GetK/GetS`, adler32 whole-tensor entry points, ReplaySSM circular commit, cvt helpers, mxfp8 v-cache update, fp8 ue8m0/hopper/transpose helpers, `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul`, `awq_gemm_triton`, rocm `tkw1`, `moe_fused_gate_jit`, inkling gate v1, `post_reorder_triton_kernel`, `fused_inplace_qknorm_across_heads`, elementwise `silu_and_mul_triton`/autotune path, `rms_normalize_triton`, stale `top_p_renorm_triton` copy, and others.
- **Legacy DSV4 compressor path removed** (`compress_old.py`, `fused_compress_triton.py`, srt `dsv4/compress_hip.py`, the old `CompressorBackendMixin`): every CUDA/HIP backend uses `compressor_v2`; `fused_norm_rope_inplace` (live) moved to `dsv4/elementwise.py`. AOT dsv4 q/k norm+RoPE ops (duplicates of the JIT ones) removed.
- **Registry (option A):** the KernelSpec inventory stays; write-only metadata goes (`FormatSignature`, `KernelSpec.format_signature/description/group/name`, `BaseFusedOp.format_signature/descriptions/dispatch_forward`, unused selector/platform helpers). `spec.CUDA_ONLY` replaces ~44 inline frozensets. Unused `BaseFusedOp`s (4 RMSNorm, Gelu/GeluTanh/ReLU2/QuickGELU) removed; facade wrappers nobody imports removed (this also fixes facade functions shadowed by same-named submodules). `Fp8ScaledMMOp` no longer declares an SM90 heuristic as a capability.
- **#42184 criteria applied** to the four remaining gate sites (route-quant, engram, vision_rope, minimax_m3): gates check eligibility, launchers enforce contracts.
- **Duplicates:** sparse-MLA decode reuses the shared kernels (bit-exact, 720 cases x 2 archs incl. fully masked rows); mxfp8 gfx95 reuses `mxfp8_quant`. Forks that are *not* bit-exact stay, each with a one-line comment (grok RMSNorm, gfx1250 qk-RMSNorm, int8 group quant on ROCm, marlin SiTU, minimax Gemma RMSNorm).
- **Test oracles shipped in op modules moved to `sglang.test.kernels`** (LPLB, dsa transform index, DCP LSE combine, dsv4 K-cache quant refs, extend attention, dspark window, multigpu launcher, mhc, per-token-group quant dispatch).

### Diffusion (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen`, -9.4K)
- **Dead code:** SenseNova-U1 unreachable chat/interleave/it2i paths (~2.6K; T2I output byte-identical), auto-residency estimators and the warmup stage-iteration calibration chain nothing read, SANA-WM parity debug harness (`SANAWM_*` env hooks incl. `torch.load` input injection), `MINIMAX_H3_USE_FUSED_NORM` path, unresolved MiniMax-H3 euler scheduler, registry subprocess-inspect path (pointed at a nonexistent module), delta-gzip realtime encoding (server + web UI), bundled-overlay lookup, `EncodingStage`, bitsandbytes 4-bit swap, `generate_with_lora` (could never run), `convert_hf_to_fp8.py`, unused platform hooks, unread `ServerArgs` fields, etc.
- **Env:** 12 `envs.py` entries nothing read removed (+ the docs rows presenting 5 of them as working knobs); raw reads of `SGLANG_ENABLE_FUSED_QKNORM_ROPE` / `MINIMAX_H3_VAE_*` declared in `envs.py` with identical parsing; unprefixed GDN dev knobs dropped.
- **Refactors (bit-exact):** `BitExactFusionGate.run()` replaces 24 hand-written verify-once/fallback blocks and the `mismatch_msg` boilerplate; one LayerNorm+modulate helper for FLUX.3/GLM/LongCat; `sites/` exports one `QualityGatedFusion` per family instead of four wrappers each (~50 facade entries, 28 imports gone). Sites that are hand-tuned for launch overhead, re-raise, verify inside the try, or differ in reference were left as they are (listed in the commit messages).

### Tests and CI
- Deleted always-skipped tests (env var set nowhere, `skipif(True)`, hard-coded dev paths), tautologies (default/literal echoes, `inspect.getsource` shape tests, log-format echoes, torch-behavior tests), duplicate cases and duplicate helpers; trimmed grids with no extra coverage (`fused_fp8_qkv_kv_cache` 1,344 -> 288 cases, AOT `moe_align` 4,368 -> 144, AOT per-token-group quant 3,632 -> 320). CI-tooling meta-tests are intentionally kept.
- New lane wiring: swapab on B200; Blackwell, SM120 and 4-GPU diffusion unit steps; 2-GPU diffusion unit files as 2-gpu standalone files; `quant-videogen` installed for its tests; comm benches no longer register no-op AMD runs; HPC-Ops tests (always skipped: the package isn't in the CI venv) disabled explicitly.
- **CI cost:** the standalone-file fix adds runners (1-GPU H100: 5 -> 6 partitions; 2-GPU: 3 -> 5 by current estimates). The estimates are 2-15x above the measured H200 times; I'll copy this PR's CI-measured values into `STANDALONE_FILE_EST_TIMES` before merge.

## Accuracy Tests

End-to-end, same GPU, fixed seed, base vs this branch (fused paths confirmed active by a gate tracer on both sides; no gate disabled):

| Model | Paths exercised | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ERNIE-Image, LongCat-Image, FLUX.2-klein-4B, Joy, MOSS-Image, Anima, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-1.3B, Helios-Distilled | `BitExactFusionGate.run`, LN+modulate helper, QK-norm+RoPE, handler-table sites, gated residual | byte-identical |
| GLM-Image (1024², 30 steps) | LN+modulate helper, QK-LN | identical to main+fix; fused == native |
| SANA 600M (512², 20 steps) | VAE fix | identical to main+fix; reproducible across processes (main is noise) |
| SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT T2I | dead-path removal | PNG md5 identical |
| Z-Image-Turbo server warmup | residency/warmup cleanup | PNG identical, same peak memory |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE decoder | lossless in-place path / exact tier | lossless identical; exact == native |

Kernel dedups were checked bit-for-bit on H200 and GB300 (scripts in the commit messages' descriptions).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No perf-path changes intended. `BitExactFusionGate.run` was not applied to the launch-overhead-tuned sites (the closures add ~160-180 ns per call on the host).

## Validation

- **H200 (sm_90):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops`, `test/registered/unit` and `multimodal_gen/test/unit` (1,624 files). Failures were re-run on main: identical failing test ids (rust extensions not built in the source tree, NPU-only, multi-GPU tests on one GPU, pre-existing diffusion kernel failures); 2 port collisions from parallel runs pass alone. 
- **GB300 (sm_103):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops` (334 files): failing ids identical to main.
- **RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120):** FA4 sm120 + FA4 + dense FA4 + sm120 paged MQA logits + sm120 fp8 linear + mxfp4 sm120 + diffusion fp8 FA sm120 + kernel namespace: all pass, same as main.
- **Multi-GPU:** every CUDA diffusion standalone file run on 2xH200 through the CI runner path (incl. `test_ar_models` and `test_diffusion_bcg_tp2_zimage_turbo` at the final head); Kandinsky 6 4-GPU cases on 4xH200.
- `pytest --collect-only` over the test trees: no new collection errors; import walk over `sglang.kernels`, `sglang.multimodal_gen`, `sglang.srt.{layers,models,...}`: no new import failures.
- **Not validated:** ROCm, NPU, XPU, MUSA (HIP-only deletions are traced through backend selection and import-checked on CUDA), a full AOT wheel link (affected TUs compiled for sm90/sm100), 4-GPU cases on Blackwell.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

items.title: [SM120] Field report: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash in production on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (PCIe, no NVLink) - working config, measured throughput, rejected topologies
items.body:
## Summary

Field data from running **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** as a production SGLang backend on **8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM120, 96 GB, PCIe-only — no NVLink)**, including the *only* topology we could get to start, measured prefill/decode, a speculative-decoding A/B, and the configuration traps that cost us real experiments. Posting because SM120 + V4.1-Flash users currently have to rediscover all of this from scratch.

Full write-up (with methodology and reproduction artifacts): https://github.com/Lei-010/hermes-agent/blob/main/docs/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-SM120-Performance-and-Production-Config.md

Related: vLLM field report https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56700 (same hardware, vLLM side), vLLM https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56892 (SM120 bug/perf tracker).

## What works

```bash
docker run --gpus all -d --name dsv41 \
  --shm-size=64g --ipc=host --network host \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -e TP_SIZE=8 -e DP_SIZE=1 -e EP_SIZE=8 \
  -e SPEC_ALGORITHM=dspark -e DSPARK_BLOCK_SIZE=6 \
  -e CHUNKED_PREFILL_SIZE=2048 \
  -v /ssd/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash:/model \
  <sglang image>
```

Effective `server_args` (verified at runtime via `/get_server_info`):

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| `tp_size` / `ep_size` / `dp_size` | 8 / 8 / 1 |
| `speculative_algorithm` | DSPARK, `speculative_dspark_block_size = 6` |
| `chunked_prefill_size` | 2048 |
| `context_length` | 1,048,576 |
| `kv_cache_dtype` | `fp8_e4m3` |
| `mem_fraction_static` | 0.72 |
| `max_running_requests` | 16 |
| `attention_backend` / `moe_runner_backend` | `dsv4` / `flashinfer_mxfp4` |
| CUDA graph decode / prefill | full (max_bs 16) / **disabled** |

**TP8/EP8 is not a preference — it is the only layout that starts** (see "Topologies SGLang rejects" below).

## Measured throughput (cold, single stream, tokens from `usage`, not SSE chunk counts)

128K cold prefill:

| Config | tok/s |
|---|---|
| `chunked_prefill_size=2048` (production) | **6,853** |
| same config re-run | 6,765 (−1.3%) |
| flashmla prefill backend | 6,845 |
| fused-MoE all-reduce | 6,828 |
| `chunked_prefill_size=4096` | 6,301 |
| `chunked_prefill_size=1024` | 6,012 |

32K prompt: ≈7,196 tok/s. GPU util ≈87% at 220 W of 600 W → **communication-bound on PCIe**, not compute-bound. ~7K tok/s looks like the ceiling for this board without NVLink.

Radix/prefix cache is the only large multiplier: cache-hit prefill **0.34 s for a 112K-token prefix ≈ 325K tok/s (≈39×)**.

Decode (client path over SSH tunnel, production config): prose 93.9 tok/s, structured/JSON 134.1 tok/s, TTFT 143–169 ms.

## DSPARK A/B (block_size=2, clean legs, each verified via `server_info` + acceptance length)

| Prompt class | DSPARK ON | DSPARK OFF |
|---|---|---|
| prose | 76.5–78.9 tok/s | 36.4–36.5 tok/s |
| structured | 120.3–120.5 tok/s | 36.5 tok/s |
| `accept len` | 3.0 tokens/step | 1.0 |

With DSPARK off the model flattens to ~36.5 tok/s regardless of prompt class — speculation is the difference between usable and unusable latency on this hardware. Production ships `block_size=6` (structured ≈237–252 tok/s vs 120 at block 2).

## Traps that cost us experiments (SGLang-specific)

1. **`--enable-expert-parallel` is a vLLM flag** — SGLang takes `ep_size`; the vLLM spelling is rejected outright.
2. **`docker run` must pass `TP_SIZE`/`DP_SIZE`/`EP_SIZE` explicitly.** Without `-e`, the container silently serves TP8 defaults and your "new" config never happens (we recorded a full sweep of false data this way before adding a config gate).
3. **`ep_size ≤ tp_size`** or the MoE rank computation divides by zero: `moe_ep_rank = tp_rank % (tp_size // moe_dp_size) // (tp_size // moe_dp_size // ep_size)`.
4. **DSPARK + DP attention requires `--enable-dp-lm-head`** — but is unreachable on this model anyway (next section).

## Topologies SGLang rejects on this model

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| DP2 × TP4 (any EP) | `ValueError: V4.1 vision currently supports TP/EP without DP, CP, PP or MoE A2A` — both replicas die within ~70 s |
| prefill context-parallel | same class of rejection |
| `--enable-dp-attention` alone | silently no DP group (`dp_size: 1`) — looks fine, isn't |

Other SM120 gaps we hit: MSCCL++ (`_tune` kernel crash), FlashInfer all-reduce fusion, `flashmla_sparse_q8`, and CUDA-graph capture for **prefill** (crashes even with DSPARK off, i.e. unrelated to speculation).

## Operational notes

- A defunct container can survive a single `docker rm -f`; the next `docker run` then fails on the name conflict while an orphaned engine process keeps the port and answers health checks — which silently mislabels the next experiment. Loop `docker rm -f` until the container is gone **and** nothing listens on the port.
- A parse failure must never satisfy an "expected config" assertion, or a server that has not started yet gets recorded as "spec disabled".
- Verify intended config from the server (`/get_server_info`) before timing anything; discard legs that fail the gate rather than recording them.

## Not established

No 24 h soak (numbers come from a working day of production use), block sizes 4/8/12 not re-measured with the fixed sweep tool, and >32K prefill/long-context degradation not characterised.

items.title: feat(jit): support native MUSA compilation
items.body:
## Overview

This PR adds native MUSA compilation to SGLang's Ninja-based JIT build path.
The MUSA branch selects `mcc`, passes `-x musa` and
`--offload-arch=mp_*`, and uses MUSA include paths and runtime libraries.
HIP retains precedence, and CUDA remains the fallback.

MUSA JIT uses C++20, aligned with the LLVM20-based mtcc20x path. CUDA and HIP
retain C++20. Shared JIT headers use the upstream C++20 facilities directly;
SGLang no longer carries a duplicate C++17 compatibility layer. The JIT cache
fingerprints the selected compiler path and version.

Runtime and FP8 aliases are supplied by TorchADA through
`stable_compat_include_dir()`. This path depends on
[yingzhou-bjtu/torchada#4](https://github.com/MooreThreads/torchada/pull/132),
currently a fork Draft. A TorchADA release containing that change is required
before this PR can be merged.

[sgl-project/sglang-omni#2442](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/2442)
is the downstream consumer integration: it exposes the existing joint-RoPE
provider on MUSA. JIT compilation remains in SGLang.

Part of #16565.

## Validation

Recorded real mtcc20x evidence: MTT S5000, LLVM20-based `mcc` (clang 20.1.8),

items.title: [Tracking] GLM-5.3-Flash on SM120: required fixes, carry status and release qualification
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] This tracks upstream integration work and outstanding fixes.
- [x] Written in English.

### Motivation

Track the fixes needed to serve GLM-5.3-Flash on two 96 GB RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs (SM120), using TP2, W4A16 routed experts, FP8 KV, vision and native MTP. Upstream main alone does not yet provide this complete configuration.

### Release and validation status

Updated 2026-09-08 for [v0.4.2](https://github.com/ormandj/sglang-glm53-flash-sm120/releases/tag/v0.4.2). The release uses official SGLang main `afe90a8bc9` and FlashInfer main `9c10d2e8f2`, with checksummed integration patches. [The release lock](https://github.com/ormandj/sglang-glm53-flash-sm120/blob/v0.4.2/stack.lock.json) identifies the exact inputs and resulting trees.

Author validation of the combined build covers changed-path CPU/GPU regressions and sanitizers, full GSM8K, C1-C4 engine measurements, cold prefill, long-context controls, forced HiCache restoration, sampled startup, and a 7680x4320 image followed by four independent cold text requests. The GHCR image was built separately from the same pinned inputs and was not separately benchmarked. [Measured behavior and limitations](https://github.com/ormandj/sglang-glm53-flash-sm120/blob/v0.4.2/BENCHMARKS.md) report the new fixed-MTP comparisons; the serving launcher retains adaptive MTP.

The release retains a 524,288-token shared device token pool. Compact native GLM FP8 rows use 528 rather than 656 bytes without requantizing values. Four concurrent requests share that pool. Host KDA lengths avoid repeated device scalar reads, and small prefill tails can use breakable graphs. These changes do not establish an isolated speedup for any individual PR.

### Submitted fixes and validation scope

- #38212 at `230102db83` includes the checkpoint-boundary, component key-cap and standalone compressed-index repairs previously reviewed at `a754a55e7b`. Its standalone CPU scope is 81 tests and 106 subtests. On the combined build, a 320-token-chunk profile passed device and confirmed host reuse at 512/768-token prefixes, plus four naturally completed coding-tool requests. Exact saved-state regressions establish checkpoint correctness; the model logprob comparisons are numerical smoke checks with unchanged control-relative bounds.
- #38213 at `342fba81d1` remains an opt-in metadata optimization with eager-reference and fallback tests. The standalone CPU checks passed three tests and six subtests. No isolated serving speedup is claimed.
- #38164 at `6fa7b61c81` retains disaggregated preallocation timeouts, empty-batch prefill-only cleanup and pending health-signal draining. Its 66 CPU tests and two subtests use mocked transport status and clocks, including two-process Gloo; they do not validate live RDMA or a standalone full model.
- The integration now uses #35645 from @imReese with tests from @Kangwenqiao, plus the published [mixed-decode sub-page follow-up](https://github.com/ormandj/sglang/commit/3878952b1bd298cbd57d792bceff083b0748e169). It replaces the earlier narrower overlapping admission guard while preserving contributor credit.

All 19 owned PR branches were rebased onto the release's audited SGLang or FlashInfer main and validated within their stated scope. The final SGLang main change was documentation-only; exact Python and test trees were checked where CPU results preceded that rebase. PR bodies identify tested heads, commands and limits. Combined-image results are separate from standalone PR validation.

## Carried upstream changes

The tables distinguish each frozen carry reference from its review head. The integration includes conflict resolutions and combined-source adaptations, so a carry reference does not imply an unchanged cherry-pick. Review status was checked on 2026-09-08. The native KV review heads were updated on 2026-09-09. FlashInfer coordination was updated on 2026-09-10; frozen v0.4.2 carry references are unchanged.

items.title: [DeepSeek-V4.1] Sequence-parallel mHC boundary and fused Engram gather/seam
items.body:
> (auto generated by Claude)

## What

Two fused paths for DeepSeek-V4.1, plus the MoE finalize plumbing they expose:

1. **mHC sequence-parallel boundary** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MHC_SP_FUSION`, opt-in): inside the sharded region each sublayer boundary becomes one collective launch — reduce-scatter of the partial sublayer output, hc post + next combine + RMSNorm on this rank's rows, all-gather of the normalized next input — with the mixing statistics produced by dedicated CTAs of the same launch (NVLS from three peers up, peer load/store at two ranks). With decoder SWA bounded replay the SP region ends at the tail boundary instead of excluding SP outright.
2. **Engram**: the hash tables shard on hash-column boundaries in symmetric memory, and the lookup defaults to an in-place gather straight into `wkv`'s MXFP8 operand — no all-reduce, no dequant/requant round trip (a bf16-dequantizing gather covers `wkv` configurations without an MXFP8 input path, exactly; the shared host table is read the same way). The gate + residual update + the next boundary's combine/norm fuse into one seam kernel with SP / DP / TP variants (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_ENGRAM_TP_FUSION_MIN_TOKENS` gates the TP variant; the image-token mask rides the kernel as a per-row skip). CUDA only; ROCm and other platforms keep the existing paths.
3. **MoE**: a raw `MoEOutput`'s finalize now defers whenever the producer supports it and lands as one fused finalize + shared-add kernel writing the caller's buffer; `get_merged` honors `out=` on the unfused arm too, fixing a path where the sequence-parallel boundary read an unwritten buffer.

## Accuracy

- Kernel level: the direct gathers are bitwise-identical to the dequantizing reference (including e8m0 zero scales and fp8 denormal payloads) on both sm90 and sm100; the DP and SP seam variants are bitwise-identical to each other across row counts, ragged splits and skip masks, including NaN/Inf injection into masked rows; 200 back-to-back SP launches show stable semaphore rotation.
- End to end (TP4/EP4, gsm8k 1319 questions, greedy): fused SP 0.9014 vs unfused 0.9113, McNemar p = 0.198 (not significant). A same-configuration rerun control scores 0.9113 / 0.9113 with only 36% exact-text agreement, i.e. the engine is not run-to-run stable at temperature 0 on this backend (as the cookbook documents), and the fused path's long-prompt logprob drift sits within that noise floor. TP-mode fusion scores 0.9052; TP2 (host table) 0.8954, all within the observed jitter band.
- The seam consumes the previous boundary's lagged `pre`, so the fused math matches the unfused operator order; equivalence rather than bitwise identity is expected against the old path (the gate's sigmoid was already approximate there).

## Notes

- TP2 cannot hold the device tables beside the weights; the host table is the deployable form there (cookbook updated, along with the gather semantics).
- Online weight updates remain rejected while derived hc weight splits are active; the probe follows the renamed stacked tensors.

items.title: GLM-5.3-Flash bug tracking
[Feature] Integrate Cake kernels via FlashInfer: model-by-model tracker
items.body:
**End-to-end validation and issue reporting:** Our shape coverage and correctness have not yet been validated end to end in model serving. If you encounter (1) end-to-end accuracy degradation, (2) unsuitable API requirements, such as unnecessarily requiring contiguous inputs, or (3) faster kernel benchmarks but worse end-to-end performance because the shapes optimized by the kernel do not cover the actual model-serving workload, please open an issue and tag @yyihuang with the affected kernel, the missing or problematic shape(s), and relevant model/serving details or a reproducer. We will resolve reported issues within **6 hours**.

## Motivation

Track integration of Cake kernels already delivered through FlashInfer into SGLang, grouped by the models that requested them. The upstream inventory is [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4254](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254); model requirements below come from its subissues and the linked implementation PRs.

The proposed integration is through FlashInfer's public/prepared APIs. Each task should connect the relevant model operator, weight/cache layout, and execution mode to an eligible kernel, then measure the complete serving path. Upstream kernel benchmarks are useful starting points, not claims of SGLang end-to-end speedup.

**Snapshot: 2026-10-03 (UTC; October 2 in US Pacific); FlashInfer main [46340689a5ab](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/46340689a5ab5665ab39f6281dac4d021d7ae94b).** “Merged” below means available in upstream FlashInfer, not necessarily in a released wheel or integrated here. Open follow-ups are explicitly marked and are not included in the merged coverage. Most listed kernels target SM100/SM103; exact architecture, SM-count, dtype, layout, and shape admission remain API-specific. Let the serving adapter retain its existing backend for configurations outside those contracts.

Notation: `T/M` = token rows, `B` = requests, `Q` = query tokens per request, `S` = KV length. MoE tuples are **(hidden size, expert intermediate size, number of experts, top-k)**; an intermediate size marked “local” is after TP sharding. Enumerated benchmark shapes are evidence points, not an assertion that every combination is supported.

## Integration and acceptance

- [ ] Pin a FlashInfer revision/release containing the required merged APIs and register backend selection at the existing operator boundary.
- [ ] Check the selected release branch separately: [#5978](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5978) is merged into `release-v0.7.1` only and reverts the BF16 head-dim-256 small-M speculative-decode route because of an intermittent B200 hang. This is a separate route from the E4M3/page-64 DCP entries below; a merge on the release branch does not establish a fix on main.
- [ ] Prepare weights, plans, output buffers, and workspaces before graph capture; account for changing request lengths, routing, state indices, and graph buckets.
- [ ] Validate each listed model/checkpoint, quantization recipe, TP/EP/CP configuration, and state/cache layout. Cover prefill, decode, speculative verification, ragged batches, and prefix-cache reuse where relevant.
- [ ] Compare against the current engine backend on model quality, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, and memory. Record the actual selected route and unsupported configurations before changing defaults.

SGLang already has model/operator boundaries for these families. Existing integration work is linked below so this tracker can be completed by extending or landing those changes.

## 1. Kimi-K3 / Kimi-K3-NVFP4 / Kimi-K3 vision

Requirements: [NVFP4 end-to-end #4568](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4568), [TP12 #4542](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4542), [ragged MLA/DCP #4658](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4658), [NVFP4 MLA #4644](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4644), [W4A8 SiTU #5156](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5156).

Start from [`kimi_k3.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py) for KDA/MLA/LatentMoE and [`kimi_k3_vl.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3_vl.py) for the vision tower. Preserve the model's layer ordering, TP reductions, state-cache semantics, and ModelOpt checkpoint preparation.

| Integration task | Covered shape / contract | FlashInfer delivery / upstream status |
|---|---|---|
| KDA prefill and fused decode | D=128. Fused one-token decode includes H=8 for TP12, plus H=12/24/32/48/96; BF16/FP32 indexed recurrent states and width-4 convolution. Prefill consumes strided q/k/v views of packed `[T,3*H*128]` projection output without densification. Prefill checkpoint outputs are BF16; FP32 checkpoints and `checkpoint_state_indices` are not admitted by the Cake prefill route. Recurrent T=1 decode with explicit `cu_seqlens` is outside the explicit Cake contract; `auto` now respects that guard. | **Merged:** `recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` and `fused_kda_decode(..., backend="cake")`; [#5551](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5551), [#5846](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5846); selector/binding updates [#5901](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5901) and [#5919](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5919) preserve the public API and served shape contracts; explicit-`cu_seqlens` auto-dispatch fix [#5760](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5760); [API](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/kda.py). |
| Dense FP8 MLA and ragged/DCP MLA | Kimi latent=512, RoPE=64, E4M3 query/cache, page=64; registered H=12/96 decode and Q<=8 MTP paths. ## Motivation

#39421.

This PR moves DeepSelect to the existing JIT infrastructure so only the required call signature is compiled for the local CUDA target.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

- Remove the DeepSelect AOT target, bindings, and explicit instantiations.
- Move the vendored kernel headers under `jit/csrc/deepselect/vendor`.
- Add a JIT C++ entry point and Python wrapper for BF16/FP32, int32/int64
  indices, normal and cluster kernels, sorting, offsets, and variable lengths.
- Keep the DeepSelect CUDA algorithm unchanged. The three kernel headers only
  drop includes of the deleted AOT `topk_select.h` files.
- Add C++ argument/storage validation, aligned output staging, and empty-batch
  handling.
- Use the JIT framework's local target directly. No `ScopedCudaDevice`, runtime
  C++ SM check, or `override_jit_cuda_arch` is added.

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling


The complete candidate path was benchmarked on NVIDIA H20 using:

- FP32 candidate logits.
- `topk_blocks=2048`.
- 20 warmup iterations.
- 100 measured iterations.
- Median latency.
- L2 cache flushing before every measured iteration.
- Two complete benchmark runs; the tables report the mean of the two medians.

The measured region includes:

```text
candidate block-score reduction
  -> candidate Top-K
  -> candidate-mask publication
  -> downstream paged Top-K
```

### Final Top-K 512

| Rows | Sequence length | PyTorch | Fused AOT | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 128K | 153.264 us | 44.112 us | 3.47x |
| 1 | 256K | 179.744 us | 63.712 us | 2.82x |
| 1 | 512K | 179.456 us | 73.888 us | 2.43x |
| 1 | 1M | 188.976 us | 96.624 us | 1.96x |
| 6 | 128K | 166.032 us | 44.064 us | 3.77x |

| 6 | 512K | 203.168 us | 73.168 us | 2.78x |
| 6 | 1M | 277.936 us | 104.672 us | 2.66x |

### Final Top-K 2048

| Rows | Sequence length | PyTorch | Fused AOT | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 128K | 154.304 us | 45.056 us | 3.42x |
| 1 | 256K | 176.864 us | 64.720 us | 2.73x |
| 1 | 512K | 179.872 us | 75.168 us | 2.39x |

- Speedup range: `1.91x–3.77x`.
- Geometric-mean speedup: `2.79x`.
- Best result: `3.77x` for 6 rows, 128K sequence length, and final Top-K 512.

The AOT Top-K kernel was also compared directly with the external DeepSelect implementation at width 131072 and Top-K 2048. The latency difference was approximately 0.3% to 0.4%, indicating that moving the kernel into `sgl-kernel` does not introduce a kernel-level performance regression.

items.title: Add triton autotune on the Mamba2 SSD kernels
items.body: ## Motivation The Mamba2 SSD Triton kernels were adapted from vLLM without their `@triton.autotune` decorators: sglang's original import (#10988) carried them commented out, and #10909 deleted the commented blocks while re-syncing the ops. The launchers still size their grids from `META["BLOCK_SIZE_*"]`, so every kernel silently ran at its signature default of `BLOCK_SIZE_* = 16` -- a 10x+ loss on the prefill kernels. Upstream vLLM has these decorators live today. ## Modifications - Restore `@triton.autotune` on `ssd_bmm`, `ssd_chunk_scan`, `ssd_chunk_state` and `ssd_state_passing`. The config lists and keys are verbatim from current `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/`, so these blocks stay diffable on the next upstream sync. - `_chunk_state_varlen_kernel` is sglang-only -- vLLM replaced it with `gather_initial_states.py` driven by `cu_chunk_seqlens` -- so it reuses the `_chunk_state_fwd_kernel` list (same tile-shape family). - Add `**autotune_cache_kwargs` (the existing sglang FLA idiom, `kernels/ops/attention/fla/utils.py`) so a tuning result survives process restarts instead of being re-measured on every server launch. - Add `prune_configs_by` / `prune_oversized_tiles`, which caps each `BLOCK_SIZE_*` at `next_power_of_2` of the dimension it tiles. A tile wider than its dimension computes a fully masked remainder over the same grid, so it is dominated. This is the fix for the `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` CI timeout -- see below. - Fix `bench_one_batch` on Mamba models: `selective_state_update` dispatches through a process-global backend that only the Scheduler installs, so every Mamba model died during decode CUDA-graph capture inside `load_model`. It is now initialized from a helper shared by `latency_test` and `correctness_test`, so `--correctness-test` is covered too. ## CI cost The 30-minute timeout on the previous run was real and caused by this PR. Autotuning is per distinct key, and `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` spans many: `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel` alone sees ~22 keys over the CI-reduced matrix (Triton folds the tensor dtypes into the key on top of `chunk_size`/`hdim`/`dstate`), at 23 configs each -- ~500 compile+bench cycles for one kernel, and ~4x that across all six. A persistent cache does not help here, since the cold pytest process never gets a hit. The prune collapses the small CI shapes to a handful of configs each (`hdim=5, dstate=5, chunk_size=16` -> 1 config; `hdim=32, dstate=32, chunk_size=8` -> 1), without touching the test matrix. ## Accuracy Tests Autotuning selects `BLOCK_SIZE_K`, which sets the K-split of the fp32 `tl.dot` accumulation, so output is **not** bit-identical to the `BLOCK_SIZE_* = 16` defaults. `lm_eval` GSM8K (5-shot), Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4, TP4: | | main | + autotune | | --- | ---: | ---: | | flexible-extract | 0.9401 ± 0.0065 | 0.9409 ± 0.0065 | | strict-match | 0.9378 ± 0.0067 | 0.9393 ± 0.0066 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling **End-to-end serving**, Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4 on GB300 TP4, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024: | Concurrency | Total tok/s (main) | Total tok/s (+autotune) | Speedup | tok/s/user (main) | tok/s/user (+autotune) | Speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 16 | 10,981 | 13,264 | **1.21x** | 104.9 | 110.2 | **1.05x** | | 32 | 15,728 | 17,751 | **1.13x** | 78.0 | 85.4 | **1.10x** | | 64 | 20,772 | 23,662 | **1.14x** | 53.0 | 59.5 | **1.12x** | | 128 | 24,877 | 29,892 | **1.20x** | 33.9 | 39.0 | **1.15x** | | 256 | 28,190 | 35,747 | **1.27x** | 20.0 | 24.3 | **1.22x** | | 512 | 29,558 | 37,776 | **1.28x** | 16.8 | 20.5 | **1.22x** | ## Checklist - This PR is rebased version of https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33937

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

SGLang's MXFP4 Marlin MoE path and DSV4 sparse MLA backend were gated to SM90 (Hopper) and SM120 (Blackwell), leaving Ada Lovelace GPUs (SM89 — RTX 4090 / L4 /L40S / L20) unable to run DeepSeek-V4-Flash via the W4A16 Marlin path. The only fallback on SM89 was load-time FP4→FP8 dequant, which materializes a full FP8 weight copy on every TP shard and OOMs at TP8 on a single 8× RTX 4090 (24 GB) node.

This PR relaxes the software hardware-gate so SM89 takes the existing Marlin + Triton sparse MLA fallback path. No new kernels are introduced; we enable pre-existing code paths that the original authors restricted to SM90/SM120 purely for testing scope, not a hard hardware limitation. The underlying Marlin MoE kernel (moe_wna16_marlin.cuh) only guards on CUDA_ARCH >= 800, and SM89 (8.9) passes that guard.

## Modifications

- **`python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`** — Add `is_sm89_supported()`, returning True only for device capability `(8,
9)`. It deliberately avoids `_check_cuda_device_version`, which matches on the major version alone and would wrongly
include Ampere SM80.

- **`python/sglang/srt/runtime_context.py`** — Register `is_sm89` as a platform probe.

- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_marlin_moe.py`** — Relax the MXFP4 Marlin MoE hardware gate from `SM90
or SM120` to `SM89 or SM90 or SM120` (safe since the Marlin kernel only requires `CUDA_ARCH >= 800`).

- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py`** — Treat SM89 like SM120 in three places:
  - `_create_flashmla_metadata` skips `sgl_kernel.flash_mla`;

  - the SM120 decode kernel (`flash_mla_with_kvcache_sm120`) is selected on SM89 as well.

(`fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch_sm120`) for multi-dim seq_lens on SM89.

- **`python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/model_hook.py`** — For DeepSeek-V4-Flash on SM89, disable Hopper/Blackwell-only

- **`test/registered/unit/utils/test_common.py`** — Add unit tests for `is_sm89_supported`: True on `(8, 9)`, False on

items.body:
## Motivation

Closes #36174.

`--enable-deterministic-inference` rejects DeepSeek-V4 at startup, and because the
model's config-time overrides pin `--attention-backend dsv4`, there is no backend to
fall back to — the flag is unusable on V4 in every configuration:

```
ValueError: Currently only ['ascend', 'fa3', 'fa4', 'flashinfer', 'intel_xpu', 'triton']
attention backends are supported for deterministic inference, but you explicitly
specified 'dsv4'.
```

Allowlisting the backend alone is not enough: with it allowlisted but nothing else
changed, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 still produces 3 distinct outputs over 20 batch sizes.
The V4 path has four separate dispatches that key off the token count.

## Modifications

Each site below picks a kernel, a tile size, or a split-K count from the number of
tokens in the batch, which is exactly what deterministic inference must not do.

1. **mHC pre-norm split-K** — `_compute_num_split_for_mhc_pre` derives `n_splits`
   from `n_sms // ceil(num_tokens / 64)`, and `n_splits` is the number of partial
   sums the K reduction is folded from, so it fixes the summation order. This is the
   first op of every layer, so a prompt prefilled alongside two others differs from
   the same prompt prefilled alone in *every* token's logprob by ~1e-2. Pinned to the
   token-independent `num_block_k // 4`. `mhc_fused_post_pre` carries the same term
   plus a `num_tokens <= 32` FMA-kernel switch, and
   `_flashinfer_mhc_pre_num_splits` is a third copy.
2. **FlashMLA sparse decode tile scheduler** — `sparse_attn_decode_interface`
   computes `payload = ceil(total_num_blocks / num_sm_parts)` over the whole batch,
   so where a request's KV range is cut depends on its co-batched requests.
   Deterministic mode issues one launch per request, which makes the schedule a
   function of that request alone.
3. **Non-paged indexer** — taken only when `batch_size == 1 and query_rows >= 8192`.
4. **Router GEMM** — `MoEGate` switches to `dsv3_router_gemm` at
   `hidden_states.shape[0] <= 16`, and `linear_bf16_fp32`'s HPC-Ops path at `M >= 8`.
   Fixing the first also fixes a startup crash: the deterministic branch of `MoEGate`
   returned bf16 router logits, and V4's fused `hash_topk` kernel requires fp32
   (`Dtype value [bfloat16] not in the allowed options: [float32]`).

Also probed and ruled out on H200, so left alone: the DeepGEMM fp8 block GEMM is
M-invariant at every V4 shape, `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` (prefill) is s_q-invariant,
and the MoE runner choice makes no difference.

Deterministic inference on `dsv4` is rejected on SM120, whose attention kernel is an
autotuned Triton kernel that picks its tile size — and with it the softmax rescaling
order — from measured timings.

Everything above is gated: with the flag off, the only changes are an extracted
`_use_sparse_prefill` predicate, two algebraically identical `max_splits` locals and
a `use_fma` local. Verified below.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, 4xH200, TP=4.

**The feature.** Distinct outputs over 32 batch sizes,
`sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode single`:

| | distinct outputs / 32 |
| --- | --- |
| without the flag | 6 |
| with `--enable-deterministic-inference` | **1** |

All three harness modes pass with radix cache and CUDA graphs on: `single` (n=32),
`prefix` + logprobs (temperature 0.5, shared prefixes of 1 / 511 / 2048 / 4097), and
`radix_cache`. Chunked prefill was checked separately at
`--chunked-prefill-size 512` over 4097-token prompts.

**No regression with the flag off.** Same box, arms run back to back, benchmark client always from `main` so only the
server tree varies.

The strongest check pins the batch at one request, which removes batch-composition
noise entirely: 150 GSM8K completions issued serially are **150/150 byte-identical**
between `main` and this branch, as are 8/8 fixed greedy prompts.

GSM8K, 400 questions, 5-shot, greedy, `--parallel 64`:

| tree | runs |
| --- | --- |
| `main` | 0.965, 0.965, 0.968, 0.968, 0.968 |
| this branch | 0.960, 0.963, 0.970, 0.960 |

Repeats within one warm server span 0.960-0.970 on this branch, bracketing every
`main` number; at 400 questions the harness cannot resolve better than about +/-4
questions. That spread is DeepSeek-V4's own batch-composition non-determinism -- the
thing the new flag removes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**With the flag off** — `sglang.benchmark.serving`, random 1024/512, 200 prompts,
concurrency 32: 

| order | tree | output tok/s | total tok/s | mean TPOT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1st | `main` | 1849.80 | 5549.39 | 14.01 ms |
| 2nd | this branch | 1919.93 | 5759.80 | 13.99 ms |
| 3rd | `main` | 1919.67 | 5759.01 | 13.99 ms |

This branch lands within 0.01% of the warm `main` run. The first run is the cold
outlier (JIT and autotune caches), and that cold-start effect (+3.8%) is far larger
than anything between the trees. `MHC prenorm prewarm: 21 n_splits buckets` is logged
by both trees with the flag off, i.e. the split-K schedule is untouched there.

**With the flag on**, decode throughput (fixed batch, 128 output tokens, best of 3):

| | bs=1 | bs=16 | bs=32 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no flag | 131 | 1611 | 3045 tok/s |
| deterministic | 50 | 354 | 444 tok/s |

Deterministic inference costs ~2.1-2.5x on its own (batch-invariant matmul/rmsnorm,
pytorch sampling, NCCL tree with pinned channels, pinned MoE and mHC split-K), flat
in batch size. The per-request FlashMLA launch adds a further 2.3x at bs=16 and 3.2x
at bs=32, and is free at bs=1. It is not optional: an ablation that keeps the single
batched launch and everything else is still non-deterministic (2 distinct outputs
over 32 batch sizes).

That ablation is also the opening for a follow-up. `sparse_decode_fwd` accepts
`tile_scheduler_metadata` and `num_splits` as inputs and only computes them when
absent, so a supplied no-split schedule would recover the single launch. This PR
takes the loop instead: it is 15 lines, obviously correct, and carries no coupling to
a pinned third-party struct layout — and its bit-exact output is the oracle a
schedule builder would be validated against.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).

items.title: [DeepSeek-V4] Enable fused and overlapped mHC stats for small SM90 decode batches
items.body:
## Motivation

On SM90, DeepSeek-V4 previously used fused mHC stats only for `M=1`.
Small decode and target-verify graphs therefore ran:

```text
partial -> reduce -> split_sinkhorn
```

on the main stream for every layer. For small `M`, this work is independent
of the following attention or MoE computation and can be hidden on the
existing mHC stats stream.

## Modifications

- Add the opt-in JSON environment variable
  `SGLANG_OPT_MHC_STATS_OVERLAP_EXTRA_TOKEN_COUNTS`.
- For explicitly enabled SM90 decode/target-verify shapes with
  `1 < M <= 16`, use the existing fused stats path:

  ```text
  partial -> reduce_sinkhorn
  ```

- Submit attention stats before attention and FFN stats before MoE on the
  existing stats stream.
- Join the stats stream only immediately before `hc_post` consumes `post`
  and `comb`.

The default allowlist is empty, so existing SM90 behavior is unchanged unless
the optimization is explicitly enabled. `M=1`, prefill, Blackwell, and the
FP4 MoE operator are unchanged.

Suggested H20 setting:

```bash
export SGLANG_OPT_MHC_STATS_OVERLAP_EXTRA_TOKEN_COUNTS='[4,8,12,16]'
```

## Accuracy Tests

- Fused-vs-unfused stats numerics passed for `M=1/4/8/12/16` with
  `torch.testing.assert_close(rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6)`.
- Maximum absolute error for every tested shape:
  `1.1920928955078125e-7`.
- Shape-policy checks passed:
  - Default: only the existing `M=1` path is enabled.
  - With `[4,8,12,16,20]`: `M=1/4/8/12/16` are enabled and `M=20`
    remains rejected by the hard cap.
- Existing mHC kernel test: 27 passed, 1 failed.
  - The failure is the existing BF16 tolerance boundary in
    `test_mhc_fused_post_pre_matches_unfused[False-17-7168]`.
  - One of 121,856 elements differs by `0.00390625` versus tolerance
    `0.002`; this test covers an unchanged operator.
- Full model accuracy evaluation was not run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Environment:

- Performance-tested base: `86cb4a0f97`
- 8x NVIDIA H20 (SM90, 97,871 MiB, 78 SMs/GPU)
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8/EP8
- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, Triton 3.6.0, FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1
- `dsv4` attention, `flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE
- Full decode CUDA graphs; prefill CUDA graphs disabled

Method:

- Random token IDs, 100 input / 128 output tokens
- Concurrency `4/8/12/16`, `4 * concurrency` requests per case
- One warmup plus five measured runs per case and variant
- Order: baseline A1 -> optimized -> baseline A2, with a fresh server and
  graph capture for every variant
- Baseline is the median of 10 A1+A2 runs; optimized is the median of 5 runs

| Decode M | Baseline tok/s | Optimized tok/s | Throughput | Baseline TPOT ms | Optimized TPOT ms | TPOT |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 199.90 | 207.38 | +3.74% | 18.311 | 17.567 | -4.06% |
| 8 | 358.34 | 367.61 | +2.59% | 20.285 | 19.727 | -2.75% |
| 12 | 469.14 | 484.80 | +3.34% | 22.227 | 21.371 | -3.85% |
| 16 | 594.56 | 600.71 | +1.03% | 23.224 | 22.935 | -1.25% |

Baseline A1-to-A2 throughput drift was `+0.23%/+0.21%/+0.16%/+0.17%`.
Optimized throughput CV was at most `0.07%`.
